records.description: The selected analysis assumes spatially flat base LambdaCDM with purely adiabatic scalar P_R(k)=A_s*(k/k_*)^(n_s-1), k_*=0.05 Mpc^-1. CAMB (August 2017) maps this prescribed initial spectrum and the adopted background, matter and thermal history to lensed CMB spectra; CosmoMC (July 2018) samples the six-parameter posterior. The base parameters are baryon and cold-dark-matter densities, theta_MC, tau, ln(10^10 A_s) and n_s, with flat base priors; the amplitude prior is 1.61 < ln(10^10 A_s) < 3.91. The adopted neutrino model has two massless states and one 0.06 eV state, BBN-predicted helium and the stated tanh reionization history. The likelihood multiplies Commander low-T, SimAll low-E and high-multipole Plik, exploring the allowed nuisance parameters jointly.
records.name: Planck base-model primordial inference
openObligations: This transfer/likelihood model includes physical lensing of TT/TE/EE but not the separate lensing-reconstruction likelihood. No BAO, BK15 or large-scale-structure likelihood is added. A power-law adiabatic initial spectrum is an assumption of this fit, not a derivation of inflation or of its quantum origin.

The hybrid likelihood neglects low/high-multipole correlations and low-T/low-E correlations; low-TE is excluded. Its high-multipole Gaussian approximation and fixed corrections carry stated limits. High-multipole amplitude is degenerate with tau through A_s*exp(-2*tau); low-E supplies conditional information on tau.

Inherited prior bounds beyond the quoted amplitude range and the full recombination, BBN, nonlinear-lensing, sampler and covariance implementations are not independently reconstructed. Other cosmologies or nuisance choices can change the posterior; no full numerical replay or unique origin mechanism is claimed.
